    16  
    17  # Augmented simplicial objects with an extra degeneracy
    18  
    19  In simplicial homotopy theory, in order to prove that the connected components
    20  of a simplicial set `X` are contractible, it suffices to construct an extra
    21  degeneracy as it is defined in *Simplicial Homotopy Theory* by Goerss-Jardine p. 190.
    22  It consists of a series of maps `π₀ X → X _⦋0⦌` and `X _⦋n⦌ → X _⦋n+1⦌` which
    23  behave formally like an extra degeneracy `σ (-1)`. It can be thought as a datum
    24  associated to the augmented simplicial set `X → π₀ X`.
    25  
    26  In this file, we adapt this definition to the case of augmented
    27  simplicial objects in any category.
    28  
    29  ## Main definitions
    30  
    31  - the structure `ExtraDegeneracy X` for any `X : SimplicialObject.Augmented C`
    32  - `ExtraDegeneracy.map`: extra degeneracies are preserved by the application of any
    33    functor `C ⥤ D`
    34  - `SSet.Augmented.StandardSimplex.extraDegeneracy`: the standard `n`-simplex has
    35    an extra degeneracy
    36  - `Arrow.AugmentedCechNerve.extraDegeneracy`: the Čech nerve of a split
    37    epimorphism has an extra degeneracy
    38  - `ExtraDegeneracy.homotopyEquiv`: in the case the category `C` is preadditive,
    39    if we have an extra degeneracy on `X : SimplicialObject.Augmented C`, then
    40    the augmentation on the alternating face map complex of `X` is a homotopy
    41    equivalence.
    42  - `ExtraDegeneracy.homotopy`: if we have an extra degeneracy `ed` on
    43    `X : SimplicialObject.Augmented C` (for any category `C`), then
    44    the morphism `X.hom ≫ ed.section_` is homotopic to `𝟙 X.left`.
